local_checks.invariant: GET /cameras and GET /cameras/{id} return only cameras inside the caller's role scope (resident: c.user_id = self; community_admin: same community AND common, own, or admin_can_view)
local_checks.result: list_cameras (cameras.py:78-83) and get_camera (cameras.py:86-95) both apply _scope (cameras.py:69-75). Every value is parameterized, and the identity comes only from the session user returned by auth.current_user; no request field overrides it. The admin predicate binds c.community_id to the session community_id. get_camera rejects anything that is not a UUID. A missing camera and an out-of-scope camera get the same 404 (_camera_not_found, app.py:695-698). No path returns a camera outside the scope.

local_checks.invariant: Only the owner of a private camera can change admin_can_view (POST /cameras/{id}/visibilidad)
local_checks.result: set_admin_visibility (cameras.py:183-191) runs UPDATE ... WHERE id = %s AND user_id = <session user> AND kind = 'private' RETURNING id. A non-owner, a common camera or a non-UUID updates no rows, and the route answers 404 (app.py:737-741). The redirect target is the UUID that was already validated. Nothing else in app.py or manage.py writes admin_can_view. CSRF on this POST is h1's coverage.

local_checks.invariant: The camera detail page shows only events and aggregates the caller may see, and the camera scope (_scope) agrees with the event scope (list_events) for each role
local_checks.result: camera_page (app.py:715-734) calls get_camera first, then list_events(user, camera_id=cam['id']), which applies the role predicate again (app.py:281-286). The count subqueries in cameras._SELECT (cameras.py:59-64) count only events of a camera that already passed the scope check. A resident's camera can only receive events from its owner (resolve_camera, cameras.py:149-162) or from its assigned edge device. The one difference: _scope admits an admin through c.kind = 'common', while list_events and the evidence query admit through c.admin_can_view. Common cameras are created with admin_can_view = true (schema default at schema_vigia.sql:138), and set_admin_visibility only changes private cameras, so this difference can only hide events, never expose them. The admin audit entry for viewing someone else's private camera is written (app.py:726-731).

local_checks.invariant: The composite (id, community_id) foreign keys make the id-only LEFT JOINs (events->cameras, media_files->cameras) community-consistent, and no camera, user or community can be reassigned
local_checks.result: cameras (user_id, community_id) -> users and (edge_device_id, community_id) -> edge_devices (schema_vigia.sql:145-148). events (user_id|camera_id, community_id) (schema_vigia.sql:169-172). media_files (user_id|camera_id|event_id, community_id) (schema_vigia.sql:192-197). Under MATCH SIMPLE a key with a NULL column is not checked, but any non-NULL camera_id must belong to the row's own community. Neither the app nor manage.py has an UPDATE that changes cameras.user_id, kind or community_id, or users.community_id, and neither deletes cameras or users. local_checks.invariant: Camera creation binds community and owner to the session, not to request fields

local_checks.invariant: limitar_subidas rejects /analyze bodies larger than MAX_UPLOAD_MB before they are received or stored
local_checks.result: upload_too_big (backend/app.py:180-186) reads only the Content-Length header, defaulting to '0' when it is absent and returning False on ValueError. A chunked request has no Content-Length and passes. FastAPI parses the whole multipart form, spooling the file part, before analyze runs, so the 200 MB counter at line 598 only limits the second copy into UPLOAD_DIR. Caddyfile sets no request_body limit, and port 8000 is also published. The same Content-Length-only pattern applies to /ingest (lines 627 and 632). engine.py analyze_video calls the shared YOLO detector and pose models without engine.infer_lock, while live sessions call them under the lock from other threads. /analyze accepts any bytes whose filename has a video extension, and cv2.VideoCapture lets the FFmpeg bundled in opencv-python-headless pick a demuxer by probing the content. Consider limiting demuxers and protocols (for example OPENCV_FFMPEG_CAPTURE_OPTIONS with protocol_whitelist;file) or checking container signatures. No exfiltration channel was found: only person-detected frames are stored, and they go back only to the uploader.

local_checks.invariant: X-Forwarded-For is accepted as client identity only from the trusted proxy (Caddy).
local_checks.result: client_ip trusts the last X-Forwarded-For element from any peer in 127/8, ::1, 10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16 or fc00::/7 (auth.py:239-240, 259-263). The result keys the login throttle (app.py:440, 449), session ip (app.py:454) and the view_camera audit ip (app.py:731). Through Caddy the last hop is the real client, since Caddy's documented default (v2.5+, image tag caddy:2) replaces client-supplied XFF. A client hitting :8000 directly is trusted only if Docker presents it from a private address, for example docker-proxy IPv6-to-IPv4 forwarding, rootless or Desktop port drivers, or a host on the same private LAN. That is a deployment fact, so this is a candidate.

local_checks.invariant: Session-issuing responses carry a Secure cookie and HSTS, and credentials travel only over TLS.
local_checks.result: Secure and HSTS both come from request.url.scheme=='https' or X-Forwarded-Proto=='https' sent by any peer (auth.py:201-209, app.py:157-158). All observed SQL is parameterized, but a future injection would run as superuser (COPY … PROGRAM). Create a least-privilege application role for DATABASE_URL.

cookie_is_secure and HSTS trust X-Forwarded-Proto from any peer (backend/auth.py:201-204), while client_ip restricts X-Forwarded-For to private peers. Today a client can only harden its own cookie, but the two trust rules should be the same: trust only the proxy.
